commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Use int64 row offsets in the K-cache gather kernels
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The DeepSeek-V4.1 K-cache gather kernels compute each output row offset in int32. Once a prefill gather chunk passes 2^31 elements, rows are written about 4 GiB outside the workspace. On MI355X, this crashes DeepSeek-V4.1 startup with DSpark adaptive verification at TP8.

This PR computes the offset in int64.

Fixes #65925.

No expected NVIDIA impact: CUDA uses the CuteDSL gather for fp8/MXFP8 (NVFP4 is already int64), so these kernels run there only as a fallback, where offsets below 2^31 are unchanged.

## Claims

- The fp8, fp8 one-pass and MXFP8 gather kernels in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/cache_utils.py` compute the row offset in int64.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 with adaptive DSpark verification now starts at TP8 on MI355X; without this change it faulted at startup in 3 of 3 runs.
- A new kernel test writes rows past 2^31 output elements. It fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Validation

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-a2bcb5657a881a002e79d0adab3c6b5e39436121` (`main` as of 2026-11-05), 8× MI355X, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`. For "this PR", the image's `cache_utils.py` with this change is mounted over the installed package.

**Reproducer:**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

| | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| base | 3 | 3/3 `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` during startup (adaptive cost profiling), 415–551 s after launch |
| this PR | 2 | 2/2 ready; `17*19` = 323; GSM8K 250, 5-shot: 0.920 (measured in 1 run); 256/256 requests at concurrency 64 |
| base, adaptive off | 1 | ready; `17*19` = 323; GSM8K 250, 5-shot: 0.932; 256/256 requests at concurrency 64 |

The serve runs used the first revision of this PR, which computed the same int64 offset inside the token loop.

**Kernel tests** (current revision, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-f5d93296c8ec82b7e7dabdb308d24d43cb1907bf`, `main` as of 2026-11-11, one GPU), `pytest -v tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py`:

| | Result |
|---|---|
| base + new test | 3 failed, 145 passed, 58 skipped. `test_v41_gather_rows_past_int32_elements[fp8 / fp8_one_pass / mxfp8]` each fail with `Test subprocess ... failed (killed by SIGABRT)` after `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`. The test runs in its own process, so the rest of the file still runs. |
| this PR | 148 passed, 58 skipped |

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** `batch_idx` is `tl.program_id(0)`, and Triton specializes `out_stride0 < 2**31` as int32, so `batch_idx * out_stride0` is int32 arithmetic.

- The ROCm prefill gathers into a `(4, M, 512)` bf16 workspace, with `M = ceil(max_model_len / compress_ratio) + window_size + max_num_batched_tokens`. `get_prefill_chunk_plan` packs requests until their area fills it.
- For compress-ratio-1 layers at the default 1M `max_model_len`, that is about 2.18e9 elements, which is more than 2^31.
- Adaptive verification's startup profile puts 511 requests with 8K context into one chunk (`out=(511, 8335, 512)`), so the last 7 requests' rows wrap about 4 GiB below the workspace.
- With `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 AMD_LOG_LEVEL=3`, the last kernel dispatched on every rank before the fault is `_dequantize_and_gather_k_one_pass_kernel` with grid `(511, 1025)`, which is this chunk.
- Whether that faults depends on what is mapped there, which is why TP4 started in our runs.

**Who hits it.** Any prefill chunk whose packed area passes 2^31 elements on a 1M-context deployment:

- the adaptive profile above
- ordinary traffic with prefix caching, such as a burst of about 140 or more requests sharing a cached ~30K-token prompt. With host-side shape logging, such a burst produced a `(140, 30159, 512)` chunk whose wrapped rows landed in the KV-cache allocation, with no visible output change in our runs.

**Scope and cost.**

- One int64 multiply per program, before the token loop, as in the NVFP4 gather; not benchmarked.
- DSv4.0's copy of these kernels keeps its workspace below 2^31 elements at normal settings and is left unchanged.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Run the fused mHC seams as AITER's single-launch HIP Mega-MHC
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On gfx950, DeepSeek-V4.1's fused delayed mHC seams now run as one launch of AITER's HIP Mega-MHC (ROCm/aiter#6520; in AITER since v0.1.27, pinned by #63774, and main now pins v0.1.29, #66596) instead of AITER's two-launch Triton seam (#58655). That covers every seam the Triton kernel serves today, including the gates that #59802 runs on the side stream.

It is a kernel-level saving: 16–41% per seam in the microbenchmark.
- **On the critical path,** profiled serving windows measure about 1% of a C256 decode step and 1.6–1.9% of a 4,096-token prefill step.
- **In serving A/Bs at n = 3 per arm,** decode (C1 to C256) and prefill-heavy alike, the change stays within run-to-run noise. That is what savings of this size predict.

Related:
- **The seam:** #58655 added the Triton seam; #59802 overlaps its gates with attention and FFN; #60153 (draft) adds a gfx942 seam.
- **The kernels:** ROCm/aiter#6520 (HIP Mega-MHC, used here) and ROCm/aiter#6179 (FlyDSL Mega-mHC). ROCm/ATOM#2568 integrates the HIP kernel in ATOM with the same pack-once design.
- **Follow-up:** the seam can also write the MXFP8 input of `wqkv_a` in the same launch; that would build on #59782 and #57857.
- **Other frameworks:** SGLang's AMD DeepSeek-V4.1 path runs its prefill and DSpark draft seams through AITER's FlyDSL Mega-mHC, behind opt-in flags (sgl-project/sglang#49283 and sgl-project/sglang#49284, open).

See Details.

## Claims

- **One launch per seam instead of two** for every fused seam on gfx950: two per decoder layer, plus the DSpark draft's.
  - **Per seam** (MI350X, this PR's benchmark, layer-30 weights, HIP-graph replay over cold inputs and weights): HIP Mega-MHC is 16–34% faster than main's Triton seam with the post block and 27–41% without. With the post block that is 2.7–5.3 µs per seam at T 1–256.
  - **In serving,** it replaces every Triton seam call, on the main stream and on #59802's side stream: the C128, C256 and prefill traces show no Triton seam kernel on any queue or rank. In those traces, the median seam takes 26–29% less time than the two Triton kernels at decode sizes, and 35% less at 4,096 tokens (54.3 against 83.5 µs).
- **Where the seam is on the critical path, it saves step time,** measured per kernel in profiled serving windows (all 8 ranks):
  - **C256 decode:** steps carry 192 tokens per rank, above the overlap's 128-token limit, so every seam runs serially with nothing else running. Mega-MHC cuts the seam from 2,069 to 1,541 µs per step (−528 µs, −25.5%), about 1.0% of the ~50.75 ms step.
  - **Prefill** (random 8192/256 at C32): prefill and mixed steps never take the overlap path, so all 86 seams of a 4,096-token step run serially and 100% exposed.
    - Mega-MHC cuts the seam from 7.1–7.5 ms to 4.6–4.7 ms per step: −2.5 to −2.8 ms.
    - That is 1.6–1.9% of the 140–177 ms step, or 0.60–0.68 ms per 1,000 prefill tokens.
  - **Elsewhere:** the seam is serial the same way in eager and PIECEWISE modes and in the draft.
- **Serving: no gain beyond noise at n = 3 per arm** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP8 + EP8, MI350X, 0 failed requests).
  - **Decode** (random 1024/1024; Nov 6, before the rebase):
    - **C128:** decode takes #59802's overlap, which keeps its post-collapse kernel on the critical path and runs the gates on the side stream, so this PR mostly shortens hidden work. The acceptance-normalized step time is unchanged (−0.02%, p 0.92). Mean ITL, which counts one streamed chunk per step and so measures the step directly, moved −0.02% too. TPOT p50's +1.5% follows the 0.7% lower DSpark acceptance length, and it sits inside the main arm's own spread (14.51–15.10 ms over its three runs). With speculative decoding off (this head, Nov 11), where TPOT is the step time, C128 TPOT p50 moves −0.05% and ITL p50 +0.01%.
    - **C256:** the acceptance-normalized step time moved −1.0% (p 0.05). That matches the trace's ~1.0%, but it sits at the noise bar.
  - **Low-concurrency decode** (this head, Nov 10; random 1024/1024 at C1, C4, C16 and C32): no metric regresses beyond noise.
    - The acceptance-normalized step time moves +0.04%, −0.07%, −0.12% and −0.29%, inside bars of ±0.5–1.1%. ITL p50 moves −0.01% to −0.31%.
    - At these sizes every decode step takes #59802's overlap. A profiled C4 window shows its post-collapse kernel unchanged on the critical path, with Mega-MHC replacing only the side-stream gates.
  - **Prefill-heavy** (this head; random 8192/256 at C32 and C64, and 4096/256 at C64):
    - **8k:** flat. TTFT p50 and input throughput change by under 3%, with p ≥ 0.26.
    - **4k at C64:** input throughput +1.45% (p 0.026) and TPOT p50 −2.7% (p 0.061). The throughput change clears twice the same-arm sd (±1.1%), but not twice the same-arm range (±2.0%).
  - **Consistent with the traces:**
    - The measured prefill saving predicts ~2% on TTFT and ~1% on input throughput for this load. That is inside the 8k configs' two-sd bars (±5.7–9.8% TTFT, ±5.9–6.4% throughput), and right at 4k/C64's ±1.1%, where +1.45% was measured.
    - The C256 decode saving predicts ~1%, where −1.0% was measured at the bar.
    - n = 3 serving on this node doesn't resolve changes of this size.
- **Numerics:** not bitwise against the Triton seam. Both do the same fp32 math with the same bf16 hi/lo split of `fn`, summed in another order.
  - **The unit test:** the residual stays within one bf16 ulp of a float64 reference, plus the fp32 summation bound. Every other output is within twice the Triton seam's relative error, plus a small floor. It passes at every tested T on MI350X and MI355X.
  - **Outside the test's T set:** on its random weights with the post block, the benchmark measures `post_mix` at 4 tokens at 3.0e-5 relative error for both HIP and FlyDSL, against 1.0e-6 for Triton.
    - The unit test passes with T 4 added (MI350X) and with T 3–8 added (MI355X). With the test's inputs, HIP's `post_mix` error at T 4 is 5.7e-6 against Triton's 5.9e-6 (MI355X).
    - So the case is specific to the benchmark's inputs; no unit test reproduces it.
  - **GSM8K** (5-shot, greedy, 1,319 questions, strict-match): 0.9227 ± 0.0074 on main and 0.9287 ± 0.0071 with this head (Nov 9). Before the rebase, the Nov 6 run gave 0.9272 ± 0.0072 and 0.9204 ± 0.0075. Both runs are within the combined stderr.
  - **GPQA Diamond** (this head, Nov 10; thinking on at `reasoning_effort` high, temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, 8 samples a question): 89.08 ± 1.35% on main and 88.64 ± 0.76% with this head (mean ± sd over 8 runs of 198; ±1.9 stderr across questions). Paired by question, the difference is −0.44 ± 0.58 points (p 0.44); the design detects about 1.6 points.
- **Weight reloads:** `fn` is packed once after loading. Every reload and in-place update reruns `process_weights_after_loading` (#65914), which refills the packs in place with `refill_derived` (#64692), so CUDA graphs captured earlier read the new weights.
- **A model-load bug** that the MI350X validation found (the server failed to start under the loader's bf16 default dtype) is fixed, with a regression test; see Validation.
- **Scope:** no new env var or config field.
  - **Where the Triton seam stays:** off gfx950, with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset or 0 (its default), and with DBO.
  - **No fallback for an old AITER:** the probe relies on the pinned AITER shipping `aiter.ops.mega_mhc`, as the Triton seam's probe relies on it for its own kernel. An AITER older than v0.1.27 now fails at load with `ModuleNotFoundError` rather than keeping the Triton seam. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` avoids that, but turns off the other AITER paths too.
  - **#59802's split is unchanged:** its post-collapse kernel stays on the critical path, and only its side-stream gates switch kernels.

## Validation

**Revisions.** Five commits, a merge of main, and a second review follow-up:
- the change, rebased onto #66397's `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.process_weights_after_loading`, which builds the mono runner first;
- the fix for the model-load bug below;
- main's docstring style (#65158), and the `mono` attribute that #66397's hook reads, set in the new bf16 test;
- the pack refill folded into `process_weights_after_loading`, since #65914 removed the `refresh_derived_weights` hook;
- the first review follow-up (Nov 10): `is_mega_mhc_available()` checks `get_cdna_version() == 4` and no longer probes for `aiter.ops.mega_mhc`, the Mega-MHC tests reuse `requires_rocm_mhc_overlap`, the float64 reference uses `sinkhorn_normalize_ref`, and `mega_mhc_prepare_stream` names its warm-up arguments;
- main `fe3ed684ce` merged in (Nov 11, `93d20795c9`). Five of its commits touch this PR's files, none in a hunk this PR changes;
- the second review follow-up (Nov 12): `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` calls `rocm_aiter_ops.mhc_mega_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm` directly instead of through a custom op that only forwarded to it, so `kernels/mhc/` is back to main's. The decoder overlap test spies on that method, and the refit test is dropped.

Which code each result ran:
- **Nov 12 unit tests (MI350X):** this head, the merge `93d20795c9` and main `fe3ed684ce`.
- **Nov 10 and 11 runs** (MI355X unit tests, GPQA, the low-concurrency decode A/B and the spec-off check): the first five commits on main `9487c9bc70` (git tree `0b0fa8b825`; the pushed fifth commit, `30f089f17e`, adds one comment line in `_aiter_ops.py` to it).
- **Nov 9 results:** the first four commits on main `8581ff0667` (git tree `7b9c7d462e`, the same diff line for line). The 16 main commits from `8581ff0667` to `9487c9bc70` touch none of this PR's files, and the fifth commit changes nothing those runs exercise with the pinned AITER on gfx950.
- **Nov 5–6 results:** the pre-rebase head plus the load fix, on AITER 0.1.27, marked as such.
- **Why the earlier serving, accuracy and trace results still apply:** the second follow-up changes only how the seam is called, and drops a test. Mega-MHC runs the same AITER function with the same arguments and packs, and the merge changes none of this PR's code paths.
- "This head" in the results below means the code that run used, as listed here.

**Hardware and software.**
- **MI350X:** 1 node, 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950, 256 CUs). Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-083fbac021348c2c7af8a7bc71ba18199d0dd7a4` (vLLM main `083fbac021`, Nov 9): torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, AITER 0.1.28.post1, MoRI 1.2.3.post1, Triton 3.8.0.
  - **Nov 9–11:** the image predates `8581ff0667` by 56 commits. Only #66397 touches this PR's files (Python only), so every arm gets it patched in, and every PR file then matches `8581ff0667` (main arm) or the PR's diff (PR arm), by md5 on every boot. The other 55, including a C++ top-k change, are absent from both arms.
  - **Nov 12 unit tests:** every `vllm/` file main changed from `083fbac021` to `fe3ed684ce` (458, this PR's included) is copied in from the arm's commit, and the 20 it deleted or renamed are removed: main's Python on the image's compiled extensions and dependencies. Each container checks those files by md5, and at the end of the run every loaded `vllm` module matches the arm's commit (only the build-time `vllm/third_party/triton_kernels` is untracked).
- **MI355X:** 1 node, 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), the same image (FlyDSL 0.4.2). Unit tests only, last run Nov 10 on the five-commit head, with #66397 patched in as on MI350X. Every file this PR touches matched that head (tree `0b0fa8b825`) by md5 in each container.

**Unit tests** in `tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py`.
- **Where they run:** like the overlap tests, they need gfx950 and AITER's fused seam (`requires_rocm_mhc_overlap`), and skip elsewhere. On gfx950 they also need the pinned AITER: without `aiter.ops.mega_mhc` they fail rather than skip.
- **CI:** the `:amd: (MI355) mHC Kernels` step runs the file. That step is optional, so it reports without blocking a merge, and it runs only when AMD CI is triggered. CI coverage of these tests therefore depends on that step being run; it hasn't run on this PR yet.
- `test_mhc_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter_mega` (24 cases): T ∈ {1, 2, 7, 48, 128, 129, 1024, 4096}, which covers the kernel's decode, split-K and single-split variants. Three call shapes: a seam with the post block, one without it (Engram, and #59802's side-stream gates), and the draft's identity pre-mix.
  - **Residual:** elementwise within one bf16 ulp of the float64 result, plus 8·2⁻²⁴ times the sum of the five terms' magnitudes (the fp32 error bound for any summation order).
  - **Every output:** its relative error against the float64 reference is at most twice the Triton seam's, plus a floor of 2⁻¹⁶ for the fp32 gates and 2⁻¹² for the bf16 outputs.
  - **Elementwise:** the same tolerances the Triton seam is held to in `test_mhc_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter_fused_rms_norm`.
- `test_deepseek_v41_rocm_mega_mhc_loads_under_bf16_default_dtype`, the regression test for the load bug below:
  - It runs the layer's `process_weights_after_loading` under `set_default_torch_dtype(torch.bfloat16)`, as the loader does.
  - It checks that the side stream's scratch was prepared, and compares both packs bit for bit with `fn` packed under fp32.
- `test_deepseek_v41_rocm_decoder_overlap_matches_serial` now also runs with packed weights (8 more cases; main's 8 now carry a `-triton` suffix).
  - The decoder layer's forward runs eager, PIECEWISE and FULL captures, as before.
  - It checks that every fused seam ran Mega-MHC (it spies on `rocm_aiter_ops.mhc_mega_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm`), including #59802's side-stream gates, whose scratch `process_weights_after_loading` allocated.
  - The replay must match the serial layer, as before.
  - Warm-up and capture now share one stream in that test, as in the model runner.
- **How the layer is built:** the bf16 and decoder tests build `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` through `__new__` and set the attributes they use, like the file's existing decoder test from main. A real one needs a full DeepSeek-V4.1 config, quantized linears and TP state.

```
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/mhc
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k "aiter_mega or mega_mhc or decoder_overlap"
```

**MI350X, Nov 12** (one session, one GPU per tree):

| tree | `tests/kernels/mhc` |
| --- | --- |
| main `fe3ed684ce` | 272 passed, 136 skipped |
| this head | 305 passed, 136 skipped |
| the merge `93d20795c9`, before the second follow-up | 306 passed, 136 skipped |

**Lint:** `pre-commit run --files` on the six changed files passes every hook on this head, including `check-docstring-style` (on Windows; markdownlint-cli2, actionlint and update-dockerfile-graph skipped).

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/_aiter_ops.py vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mhc.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py \
  tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mhc_seam_rocm.py
```

**Where the seam sits, and what Mega-MHC saves** (Nov 9, this head; one profiled window per arm).
- **Config:** the decode serving setup below on the Nov 9 MI350X image, random 1024/1024 at C256 (1024 prompts, 192 rows per rank per decode step). 40 iterations starting 300 in, all 8 ranks.
- **"Exposed" time** is the part of a kernel during which no kernel runs on any other HW queue. MoRI's dispatch and combine kernels spin while they wait, so they don't count as concurrent work.

| per decode step, mean over the 8 ranks | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| seam launches | 85.5 (171 Triton kernels) | 85.5 `mega_mhc_kernel` |
| Triton seam kernels (`_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rmsnorm_main/reduce_kernel`) | 171.1 | **0** |
| #59802's post-collapse kernel (the overlap path) | 0 | 0 |
| seam µs per step, mean ± sd over ranks (range) | 2,069 ± 56 (1,994–2,151) | 1,541 ± 68 (1,465–1,637) |
| of which exposed (on the critical path) | 2,069 (100%) | 1,541 (100%) |
| µs per seam (median) | 13.8 + 8.0 = 21.8 | 16.2 |

- **At C256 the seam is entirely on the critical path.** Decode steps carry 192 tokens per rank, above the overlap's 128-token limit, so neither arm takes #59802's overlap path, and nothing runs on any other queue while a seam does.
- **Mega-MHC replaces every seam call:** 85.5 launches a step, as many as main's Triton pairs, and no Triton seam kernel on any queue or rank.
- **It saves 528 µs per step,** −25.5% of the seam's time.
  - Against the step (mean TPOT × DSpark acceptance length: 50.75 ms for main, in an unprofiled C256 run in the same boot), that is **~1.0% of step time**.
  - The Nov 6 estimate from the microbenchmark was 0.3–0.5 ms.
- **The unprofiled C256 runs in the same boots** (n = 1 per arm, not a verdict): main 10,999 tok/s, TPOT p50 19.64 ms, step 50.75 ms; this PR 11,219 tok/s, 19.39 ms, 49.86 ms.
- **The side stream** (C128, this head only: 512 prompts, 96 rows per rank, where decode takes the overlap path):
  - #59802's post-collapse kernel ran on 57.8 of the 85.3 seams a step (6.1 µs each, fully exposed).
  - `mega_mhc_kernel` ran 85.3 times a step (12.1 µs each), again with no Triton seam kernel on any queue or rank. So the overlapped seams' side-stream gates run Mega-MHC too.
  - Only 59% of Mega-MHC's time is exposed at C128, because the overlapped gates are hidden behind the critical path. That is why C128 decode gains little.

**Profiled prefill window: the seam on the critical path of 4,096-token steps** (Nov 9, this head; the Nov 9 MI350X image and arms above).
- **Workload:** random 8192 in / 256 out at C32 (128 prompts), the prefill A/B's first config, after a 32-prompt 8k warm-up. The torch profiler covered the first 250 engine steps of the run: the opening burst of 4,096-token prefill chunks, its decode, and the next wave's prefills.
- **Runs:** main, this PR, this PR, main, with a fresh server each: n = 2 windows per arm, 1,992 rank-steps each. The installed files had the same md5s on every boot.
- **Method:**
  - **Step types:** each step's prefill and decode tokens come from vLLM's per-step annotation (`execute_context_N(prefill tokens)_generation_M(decode tokens)`).
  - **Step time:** a step runs from its forward's first mHC kernel to the next forward's.
  - **"Exposed" time:** as above.

| per rank-step, median (two windows per arm) | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| **pure prefill, 4,096 tokens** (14–16 rank-steps per window) | | |
| seam µs per step, total = exposed | 7,292 / 7,547 | **4,591 / 4,680** |
| µs per seam (86 per step) | 68.8 + 14.7 = 83.5 (Triton main + reduce) | 54.3 (Mega-MHC) |
| step time ms (GPU-busy ≈ period) | 174.0 / 177.3 | 164.9 / 166.8 |
| GPU work outside MoRI's waits, ms | 106.1 / 105.9 | 101.2 / 101.4 |
| **mixed, ~4,082 prefill + ~14 decode tokens** (98–106 rank-steps) | | |
| seam µs per step, total = exposed | 7,166 / 7,148 | **4,677 / 4,723** |
| step time ms | 139.8 / 141.9 | 130.5 / 132.3 |
| **decode, 24 tokens** (~1,840 rank-steps) | | |
| seam µs per step: total / exposed | 1,221 / 370; 1,227 / 373 | 913 / 365; 902 / 356 |
| #59802's post-collapse kernels per step (the overlap path) | 62.9 / 64.6 | 57.9 / 61.5 |
| step time ms (GPU-busy) | 31.5 / 31.0 | 30.5 / 30.2 |

- **The overlap path doesn't apply to prefill.**
  - There are 0 post-collapse kernels in every prefill or mixed step: above 128 tokens, and even in mixed steps of up to 128 tokens.
  - So every seam runs serially, 100% exposed, on the critical path.
  - Decode steps (24 tokens) take the overlap path, which hides all but ~370 µs of the seam.
- **Mega-MHC replaced every seam call.** This PR's windows have 0 Triton seam kernels in any step type, against ~339,000 in each main window. All 86 seam launches per 4k step are `mega_mhc_kernel`, on every HIP stream the windows used.
- **The measured critical-path saving per 4,096-token prefill step:**
  - **2.8 ms** in pure prefill and **2.5 ms** in mixed steps;
  - that is 0.60–0.68 ms per 1,000 prefill tokens, −34% to −37% of the seam;
  - and 1.6–1.9% of the 4k step's time (140–177 ms), or 2.6–2.7% of its GPU work outside MoRI's waits.

  - Thinking on with `reasoning_effort` high (RFC #59665); temperature 0.6 and top_p 0.95 (as #60397); 65,536 max tokens; 256 requests in flight.
  - 8 samples a question, 1,584 per arm, split 3 + 3 + 2 repeats over each arm's three boots. A request's seed depends only on its question and repeat, so it is the same in both arms.
  - Only the answer after `</think>` is graded; a response cut at 65,536 tokens scores 0.

| | main | this head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| per run (repeats 0–7), % | 90.91 / 87.37 / 87.88 / 89.39 / 88.89 / 90.91 / 87.88 / 89.39 | 87.37 / 88.89 / 87.88 / 88.89 / 89.90 / 88.89 / 88.38 / 88.89 |
| mean ± sd over runs | 89.08 ± 1.35 | 88.64 ± 0.76 |
| stderr across questions | ±1.90 | ±1.91 |
| cut at 65,536 tokens | 45 (2.8%) | 57 (3.6%) |
| accuracy without the cut responses | 91.68% | 91.94% |
| output tokens, median / mean | 2,889 / 8,847 | 2,944 / 9,316 |

- **Difference: −0.44 points, not significant.**
  - Paired by question: −0.44 ± 0.58 points (p 0.44; 95% CI −1.6 to +0.7).
  - Welch t over the 8 runs: p 0.44.
  - Pooled binomial over 1,584 samples per arm: p 0.69. That test is conservative, because both arms answer the same questions.
- **What the design detects** (α 0.05, power 0.8): about 1.6 points paired by question, 1.5 over the runs, and 3.1 with the pooled binomial.
- **Most of the gap is responses cut at 65,536 tokens.** This head has 12 more (p 0.23, so within noise): 20 questions against 22 on main, 15 of them shared. Without the cut responses, the arms are 91.68% and 91.94%.

**Trace at C128** (Nov 6, one profiled window per arm, 40 iterations starting 300 in, all 8 ranks).

| kernel class, per iteration (mean over ranks) | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Triton seam: `_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rmsnorm_main_kernel` / `..._reduce_kernel` | 85.1 / 85.1 (10.4 / 9.0 µs each) | **0 / 0** |
| `mega_mhc_kernel` (3 template variants) | 0 | 85.2 (13.8 µs each) |
| `_mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_kernel` (#59802's overlap path) | 71.9 (6.1 µs each) | 56.1 (6.1 µs each) |

- **Per seam:** 13.8 µs against 19.4 µs for the two Triton kernels (−29%).
- **The overlap path is unchanged.** #59802's post-collapse kernel still runs on the overlapped decode steps; its count differs between the windows because their batch mixes differ.
- The trace's kernel "tid"s are HIP hardware queues, which several streams share, so the per-stream claim rests on the zero Triton count rather than on queue IDs.

**Caveats.**
- **GPUs:** everything ran on MI350X except the unit tests, which also ran on MI355X (last on Nov 10, on the five-commit head; not rerun on this head). There is no MI355X benchmark or serving run. CI's optional `:amd: (MI355) mHC Kernels` step runs the unit tests once AMD CI is triggered.
- **Revisions:** the results ran different heads, from the pre-rebase head (Nov 5–6, AITER 0.1.27) to this one (Nov 12 unit tests); see Revisions for which, and why the earlier evidence carries over.
- **Base:** the Nov 9–11 MI350X runs lack 55 of main's commits up to `8581ff0667`, in both arms. The Nov 12 unit tests run main `fe3ed684ce`'s Python on the image's compiled extensions (see Hardware and software).
- **Patches:** every serving arm carries the Engram registration patch.
- **Load:** a synthetic random dataset (DSpark acceptance length ~2.5), and n = 3 per arm. At an expected ~1%, that n doesn't resolve the serving change on this node.

## Details

**Why one launch pays.** The Triton seam is a split-K main kernel followed by a per-token reduce.
- **What the second launch costs:** a launch, the gap between the two kernels, and a round trip of the partials through memory.
- **Mega-MHC:** the last workgroup to arrive sums the partials in the same launch.
- **When it counts:** the saving is mostly fixed per seam, so it counts fully at decode batch sizes.
  - It shortens the step where the seam is on the critical path: eager, PIECEWISE, more than 128 tokens per rank, and the draft. The C256 decode and 4,096-token prefill traces measure that case.
  - On #59802's side stream it only frees CUs that attention and FFN share.

**Why HIP rather than FlyDSL.** Both are AITER kernels with the Triton seam's arguments and outputs.

| | HIP Mega-MHC (`aiter.ops.mega_mhc`) | FlyDSL Mega-mHC (`aiter.ops.flydsl.mega_mhc_kernels`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weights | public `mega_mhc_shuffle_fn(fn)` pack, passed with `w_preshuffle_bf16=True` | packs `fn` internally, cached by tensor id and version counter; no public pack |
| Arch | tuned gfx950 kernels for H 5120 and 7168 on 256 CUs; a generic kernel for gfx942 and other shapes | gfx950 only |
| Build | HIP, prebuilt in the ROCm base image (`PREBUILD_KERNELS=1`) | FlyDSL, JIT-compiled on first use for each launch config, which depends on T (not in AITER's FlyDSL AOT set) |
| Outputs | BF16, or BF16 plus MXFP8 codes and E8M0 scales | BF16, fp8-grid BF16, or MXFP8 |
| Numerics | FP32 accumulation of a bf16 hi/lo `fn`, like the Triton seam | the same |
| Speed vs FlyDSL (aiter#6520, gfx950, eager) | 1.12x at T ≤ 8, 0.94–0.99x at T 16–256, 1.00–1.21x above | |

- **The weight pack decides it.** FlyDSL's cache misses an in-place update that bypasses the version counter (`param.data.copy_()`). When it does repack, it allocates a new tensor, which graphs captured earlier don't see. With HIP's public pack, vLLM owns the packed tensor and can refill it in place (`refill_derived`).
- **Measured on AITER v0.1.27 / FlyDSL 0.4.0** (MI350X, this PR's benchmark):
  - FlyDSL / HIP over T 48–256 has a median of 0.99 with the post block and 1.06 without, across three weight sets.
  - FlyDSL is clearly faster only at T 256 with the post block (0.84–0.86), so HIP stays.
  - Switching later would only need AITER to accept HIP's pack, whose bytes match FlyDSL's internal one.

**Changes** (+193/−3 in four `vllm/` files, +211/−20 in the test file, and a new 466-line benchmark).
- **`vllm/_aiter_ops.py`:**
  - `is_mega_mhc_available()`: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` and `get_cdna_version() == 4` (gfx950). It relies on the pinned AITER for `aiter.ops.mega_mhc`.
  - `mega_mhc_pack_fn()`.
  - `mhc_mega_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm()`, the same contract as `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm()` but with the packed weight.
  - `mega_mhc_prepare_stream()`: one eager call on zero weights, created as fp32 whatever the default dtype. Its gate and Sinkhorn arguments are arbitrary, since AITER sizes the scratch from the device, the stream, the token count and the hidden size only.
- **The test file:** the new tests reuse the overlap tests' `requires_rocm_mhc_overlap`, whose definition moves above them, unchanged (14 of the −20 lines).
- **`layers/mhc.py`:** `MHCPreDelayedOp` takes an optional `fn_packed`.
  - The fused ROCm branch calls `rocm_aiter_ops.mhc_mega_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm` when it is given and the norm weight is bf16, and otherwise the Triton seam's op.
  - No custom op: DeepSeek-V4.1 isn't torch.compiled, and no graph pass matches mHC ops.
  - Other paths ignore it.
  - Eligibility is decided before the launch, and no exception falls back.
- **`models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`:**
  - `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` decides `use_mega_mhc` once: fused seams, `hc_mult` 4, no DBO, and the probe.
  - `process_weights_after_loading`, after main's mono runner build, packs `hc_attn_fn` and `hc_ffn_fn`, and refills the packs in place when it reruns: every reload and in-place update ends there (#65914). It also prepares the side stream's scratch.
  - The 4-stream seams pass the pack. Layer 0's broadcast entry projects `x` and is unchanged.
- **`models/deepseek_v41/amd/mhc.py`:** `mhc_pre_delayed_overlap` passes the pack to both of its calls. `MHCOverlapStream.prepare_mega_mhc` allocates the side stream's scratch, once.
- **`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mhc_seam_rocm.py`:** new; see Validation.

**CUDA graphs.** Mega-MHC keeps its split-K scratch (and counters it re-arms itself) per stream, and refuses to allocate it during capture.
- **The main stream:** vLLM's eager profile and warm-up runs use the capture stream at the largest token count, so its scratch exists before capture.
- **The side stream:** #59802's gates run there only inside FULL capture. So the first layer's `process_weights_after_loading` makes one eager call on that stream: 128 tokens of zeros, which sizes the scratch for every batch the overlap captures.
- **Precedent:** #60153's warm-up makes a similar dummy call.

**#59802 and bitwise equality.** #59802's main-stream kernel copies the Triton seam's expression order, so its residual is bit-identical to the serial seam's.
- **With Mega-MHC:** the serial seam rounds the same fp32 sum in another order, so the overlapped and serial residuals can differ by one bf16 ulp. The gates differ by the corresponding fp32 noise.
- **The existing test:** its bitwise overlap test still covers the Triton pairing, since it passes no pack.
- **The new coverage:** the decoder test covers the Mega-MHC pairing at its existing tolerance.
- **Not in this PR:** a variant of the post-collapse kernel in Mega-MHC's order (x·post, then an fma over the four streams) would make the two paths bitwise equal again.

**Limitations and tradeoffs.**
- **Memory:** each pack is the size of `fn`, about 2 MB at H 5120, and there are two per decoder layer: ~160 MB per GPU for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's 40 layers. This is allocated during loading, before KV-cache sizing. `fn` itself stays, for the Triton fallback and #59802's path.
- **gfx950 only.** The generic HIP kernel would also run on gfx942, but it is unmeasured there; #60153 adds a different gfx942 path.
- **DBO:** excluded, because its ubatch streams don't guarantee eager warm-up on the capture stream. The overlap is excluded under DBO for its own reasons.
- **Env gating:** like the other `_aiter_ops` probes (the FlyDSL GDN prefill probe, for one), it needs `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER`.
  - So `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` is the switch back to today's seam, without a new env var.
  - The Triton seam itself runs whenever AITER is found, so users who don't set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` keep it. The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe sets it on AMD.
- **`--monokernel`:** decode steps the mono layer takes (up to 48 rows) run its own seam, not either of these. #65421 (open) would add asm decode layers with their own seams for 17–256-row steps at TP4 under `--monokernel`.
- **Sleep mode:** untested. Like `rocm_block32_gemm`'s split-K counters, Mega-MHC keeps persistent per-stream counters.
- **JIT build:** an AITER wheel built without the prebuilt `module_mega_mhc_stream_*` JIT-builds it once on first use.

**Interplay with open PRs.**
- **#60153:** the gfx942 seam, where `fn_packed` is never built. It touches lines next to this PR's in `_aiter_ops.py` and the top of `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip`; whichever merges second rebases.
- **#65526:** moves `finalize_mhc_broadcast_weights` to `refill_derived`, the pattern used here, and adds the same `refill_derived` import to `amd/model.py`; whichever merges second drops one line.
- **#65521:** FlashInfer mega mHC for `MHCFusedPostPreOp` on CUDA. Independent; it doesn't overlap this PR's hunks.

**Not duplicated** (searched 2026-11-09):
- **Command:** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "<q> updated:>=2026-11-05"`, extending the 2026-11-05 search (which covered `updated:>=2026-09-15`), with q in: "mega mhc", Mega-MHC, mega_mhc, "mhc seam", mhc_fused_post_pre, mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed, "flydsl mhc", flydsl mega, "mhc rocm", "mhc aiter", "mhc gfx950", mega_mhc_shuffle_fn, MHCPreDelayedOp, "delayed mhc", mhc_pre_delayed, "deepseek v4.1 mhc", "mhc overlap", hc_attn_fn, prepare_mega_mhc, "single-launch" mhc.
- **Issues:** `gh issue list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "<q> updated:>=2026-11-05"` for "mega mhc", "mhc rocm", "mhc aiter", mega_mhc and Mega-MHC.
- **Findings:** still no other PR or issue wires either AITER Mega-MHC kernel into vLLM.
  - **CUDA:** the Mega-mHC PRs are #56962 (DeepGEMM, merged), #65521 (FlashInfer, open) and #65069 (batch invariance, draft). The new mHC PRs since 2026-11-05 are CUDA too: #66140 (mHC post for small SM100 batches), #66142 (SM100 input-norm stores) and #66652 (CuTe DSL mHC boundary for decode-size batches, SM100).
  - **ROCm:** the seam PRs are #58655 and #59802 (merged), which this PR builds on, and #60153 (gfx942, draft). #65421 (open) runs its own seams inside asm decode layers and doesn't touch this seam's kernels.
  - **Reload:** #58995 (hyper-connection buffer refresh on weight reload) touches `finalize_mhc_broadcast_weights`, not the seam.

**Earlier evidence (not on main).**
- **An earlier FlyDSL-based revision** gained 2.4% output throughput on an agentic C128 workload, measured before #59802's overlap existed; the overlap now hides most of the seam at that size.
- **ATOM:** ROCm/ATOM#2568 measured HIP Mega-MHC in ATOM (TP4, C256): +1.7% total throughput, n = 1.

**AI assistance:** AI tools (Claude, in Cursor) helped port the change onto main, compare the two AITER kernels, write the tests and the benchmark, run the MI350X and MI355X validation on my machines, find and fix the model-load bug, search for overlapping work, and draft this description. I have reviewed every changed line and the validation logs. The commits carry a `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Allow DeepGEMM/Triton block-FP8 MoE with FlashInfer NVLink all2all
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`--moe-backend deep_gemm` maps to `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts`, a fallback expert class that needs both `DeepGemmExperts` and `TritonExperts` to accept the parallel config. Both reject the FlashInfer NVLink one- and two-sided all2all. The DeepGEMM gate carries `# NOTE(rob): discovered an IMA with this combination. Needs investigation.` (added in vllm-project/vllm#32567). The Triton gate has no comment. No issue or reproducer for the IMA was found.

This PR lets both classes run with the one- and two-sided kernels, and fixes the two-sided expert-id bug that made those combinations fail (see below).

## Test Plan

GLM-5.3 FP8 on GB300. Agentic rollout benchmark: ~30k in / 6k out, 24 turns, GRPO n=8. GSM8K (n=123, greedy) before and after a KV-cache flood.

## Test Result

DEP8 on 2x4 GB300, `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`, sync pynccl EPLB (16 redundant experts), `--max-num-batched-tokens 448`, g64. Arms ran in alternating order.

| arm | run 1 | run 2 |
|---|---|---|
| default MoE (TRT-LLM FP8) | 832.2 | 836.9 |
| `--moe-backend deep_gemm` (this PR) | 852.4 | 856.7 (+2.4%) |

On Blackwell `is_deep_gemm_e8m0_used()` is true, so `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts` always picks DeepGEMM. To cover `TritonExperts` directly, we ran DEP4 on one node with `--moe-backend triton`:

| all2all | MoE backend | result | GSM8K before / after flood |
|---|---|---|---|
| one-sided | deep_gemm | OK | .927 / .911 |
| one-sided | triton | OK | .911 / .894 |
| two-sided | triton | garbage output | 0.0 / 0.0 |
| two-sided | deep_gemm | startup failure (DeepGEMM JIT `cuKernelGetFunction` panic) | n/a |

- No IMA in any one-sided arm: 5 two-node, 3 single-node.
- The two-sided rows above are before the fix below.

### Two-sided root cause (fixed here)

FlashInfer two-sided prepare marks padding slots (rows past a source rank's token count) with `invalid_expert_id`. `FlashInferNVLinkTwoSidedManager` set it to `num_experts`, but `moe_sum` / `apply_expert_map` only skip ids `< 0`, so `expert_map[num_experts]` reads past the map: garbage with Triton, illegal address with DeepGEMM. The one-sided manager already uses FlashInfer's default `-1` (SGLang also passes `-1` for DeepGEMM and TRT-LLM). This PR sets the two-sided manager to `-1` as well.

With this fix, two-sided + `--moe-backend triton` gives GSM8K .878 / .886 (was 0.0), and two-sided + `--moe-backend deep_gemm` starts and gives GSM8K .935 / .927 (709 tok/s/GPU, single node g32), so the two-sided gates in `_supports_parallel_config` are removed too.

## Risk

The original IMA report was not reproduced. Other models and quant schemes are not covered by these runs.

commits.pr_title: [Core][MM] Make the multimodal encoder cache size configurable
commits.pr_body:
## Motivation

- **What:** `SchedulerConfig.encoder_cache_size` is derived from `max_num_batched_tokens` and is `Field(init=False)` with a standing `# TODO (ywang96): Make this configurable.` This adds `--encoder-cache-size`. `None` keeps today's derivation, so **no behaviour change unless it is set**.
- **Why:** they are different quantities. `max_num_encoder_input_tokens` is a per-step **compute** budget; `encoder_cache_size` is a **capacity** for keeping encoder output resident *across requests*, so a later request on the same image can skip the encoder (`EncoderCacheManager.check_and_update_cache`).
- **Cost today:** cross-request reuse is capped at `max_num_batched_tokens / tokens_per_item` items and cannot be raised on its own. Production document parsing sends two requests per page against the same image; past that cap the second one re-encodes the whole image.
- **Profiling fix, required by the new setting:** `get_encoder_budget()` = `min(compute, cache)` feeds how many dummy items `profile_encoder_cache` leaves resident, so a cache above the compute budget is under-reserved and the surplus is handed to the KV cache. `reserve_encoder_cache_residency()` tops it up at all three profiling sites (MRV2 / MRV1 / CPU). The dummy *compute* batch is untouched, so the profiled activation peak is unchanged; `get_encoder_budget()` itself is unchanged, since it also bounds `mm_max_items_per_batch`.
- **Kept:** the `max(..., max_tokens_per_mm_item)` floor — without it `_validate_model_input` starts rejecting those requests — now warning when it overrides an explicit value.
- **Memory:** the capacity is logged in GiB as well as tokens. The cached tensor is the multimodal embedding width (~2 KiB/token at 1024-wide, ~7 KiB at 3584-wide), which is model-dependent and is why the default is left alone.
- **Out of scope:** `max_num_encoder_input_tokens` (same TODO, separate decision); `vllm:encoder_cache_*` metrics (none exist today); the block-aligned prefix-hit interaction, where a hit skips the encoder only if it covers an item's entire placeholder range.

## Validation

- **Single variable:** `--encoder-cache-size 65536` vs unset. `--max-num-batched-tokens` stays at 16384 and prefix caching stays off in every run.
- **Confirmed before measuring:** `compute_mm_encoder_budget` returns `(16384, 16384)` without the flag and `(16384, 65536)` with it, and startup logs show `can hold 16384 tokens ... (0.03 GiB)` vs `can hold 65536 tokens ... (0.12 GiB)`.
- **Setup:** 1x H100 80GB, exclusive (0 MiB / no foreign process at boot, re-checked around every timed region), vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev229+g3966924d5` + this patch, bf16, TP=1. Real 150-DPI document pages (~2,050 image tokens), 200 page-pairs per run at concurrency 16, each worker sending the full-page request and then the coordinate request for the same image.
- **Method:** the comparison was run **3times,** restarting the engine for each configuration. Numbers below are averages. Noise is at level ~4.6% (second-pass E2E) and ~4.3% (pages/s).

| | baseline | `--encoder-cache-size 65536` | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| second-pass E2E | 0.478 s | 0.378 s | **-21.0%** |
| pipeline pages/s | 5.34 | 6.34 | **+19.0%** |
| second-pass TTFT | 0.123 s | 0.072 s | **-41.9%** |
| unique-page pages/s (no reuse possible) | 7.72 | 7.69 | -0.4% (inside noise) |

Mechanism, from the earlier run that moved `max_num_batched_tokens` (the only lever available before this patch) — second-pass TTFT in ms across concurrency:

| cache | c=1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16384 (~8 items) | 41 | 42 | 43 | **77** | **100** | 98 |
| 65536 (~32 items) | 40 | 41 | 44 | 49 | 52 | **78** |

Each knee lands at `encoder_cache_size / tokens_per_item` and moves 4x when the cache does; below the knee the two are indistinguishable (<=3.5%, inside noise), which is the control — the setting cannot act until the working set exceeds the cache. `ΔE2E = ΔTTFT + ΔTPOT x tokens` accounts for 103% / 99% / 110% of the measured delta at c=8/16/32: about half from the encoder leaving the second request's critical path, half from cheaper decode once the GPU stops re-encoding other in-flight pages. That earlier bundled change gave -19.9% / +16.9%, slightly *less* than changing the cache alone, so its batch-budget half contributed nothing.

**Tests.** 5 in `tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py` (default derivation; capacity independent of the compute budget; floor to the largest item; `ge=1`; and that cross-request reuse survives exactly while capacity allows) and 3 in `tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py` for the residency helper (reserves exactly the shortfall / no-op when the dummy batch already fills the cache / tolerates an empty batch). Both files are already tethered and this diff triggers both steps: `pytest -m 'cpu_test' v1/core` on `cpu-small`, and `V1 Executor + Worker` (H200) via `pytest -v -s v1/worker`. Locally 27 passed in the first file (22 pre-existing + 5 new) and the 3 helper tests pass; `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` shows 5 failures that reproduce identically on the unpatched base. Full `pre-commit` passes, including mypy.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Keep dummy FP8 weights within +-1 in the HiSparse e2e tests
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`(H200 MIG 18GB) E2E Core` Shard 1/2 has failed on every main build since [102833](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102833) (last pass 102828), including nightly 102861. All 5 `v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py` tests fail, for example:

```
test_hisparse_terminal_prefix_reuse - assert [113452] == [88396]
```

#67693 ("Fill dummy FP8 weights with random codes across the range") made the dummy loader fill 8-bit float params with random codes across the whole FP8 range, about 130x larger than before. These tests run a shrunk dummy DeepSeek-V3.2 and compare greedy tokens between paths that aren't bitwise equivalent: cold vs. restored prefix, batched vs. single, two engines. With full-range weights the dummy model's logits are near-ties that flip on kernel-level noise, so even the cold-path tokens differ between builds. #67693's own PR build (102832) failed the same way.

The fix adds an autouse fixture in this test file that passes `low=-1, high=1` for 8-bit float params, the loader's documented opt-out from the full-range fill. The engine runs in-process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) in a forked child, so the patch applies to the model these tests load. It's a test-only change; the loader is untouched.

Trade-off: with ±1 weights these tests exercise KV correctness less sharply. The alternative is to compare logprobs with a tolerance in each test. #67693 also broke the B200 Fusion E2E Config Sweep tolerance in the same way, so its author (WoosukKwon) may prefer a loader-side change instead, such as keeping scale-like FP8 params narrow.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for "hisparse" and "dummy fp8" and found none.

## Test Plan

- CI: `e2e-core-1-gpu` (H200 MIG 18GB), as a selected-steps build on this PR.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`

## Test Result

- pre-commit passes.
- GPU: [build 102873](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102873), `e2e-core-1-gpu` (H200 MIG 18GB): both shards passed. All `test_hisparse.py` tests passed in Shard 1/2 (5/5 failed on main).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed the change.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes a port-reservation race that makes `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e.py` fail intermittently in the `:amd: (MI355 DPX) V1 KV Offload` CI job with `ZMQError: Address already in use`. This changes only the test file.

## Claims

- The P2P lifecycle e2e tests no longer release their ZMQ control ports before the engines bind them. Each port stays reserved from fixture setup until teardown.
- This removes the `Address already in use` failures seen in Buildkite builds [102329](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102329) (consumer bind on `127.0.0.1:59279`) and [101771](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101771) (spawned producer bind on 43813, then `_queue.Empty` after 180 s).
- No production code, timeouts or checks are changed.

## Validation

| Check | Command / setup | Before (origin/main `3d091b6f05`) | After (`5206817910`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU e2e under ephemeral-port churn (MI355X, flock) | `pytest -v -s v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e.py` with a churner that keeps 8000 ephemeral loopback listeners rotating | 3/3 runs failed (5/6 test executions failed), all with `Address already in use` | 5/5 runs passed (10/10 test executions) |
| Independent review rerun (same churn, different GPU) | same as above | 3/3 runs failed, `Address already in use` in every log | 3/3 runs passed (6/6 tests), 0 `Address already in use` hits |
| GPU e2e without churn | same file, no churner | 2 passed (48 s) | 2/2 runs passed |
| Counted CPU race | pick port, churn ephemeral listeners for 0.5 s, then bind `ZmqTransport` | 19/100 binds failed with `Address already in use` | 0/100 failed |
| Mechanism check (CPU) | hold a reservation, do port-0 binds | n/a | 0/20000 port-0 binds landed on the reserved port, and `ZmqTransport` then bound it and accepted a TCP connect. A spawned child process could also bind the parent's reserved port. |
| Lint | `uvx pre-commit run --files tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e.py` | n/a | all hooks passed |

At a lighter churn of 2000 listeners, 3/3 runs on main passed. That fits a timing race that only shows up under enough port pressure, which the CI host provides through the test's own NIXL/UCX, torch.distributed and engine sockets.

## Details

**Root cause.** The `p2p_control_peer` fixture, `test_inference_reuses_a_finished_kv_request_id` and `test_inference_uses_completion_buffered_after_disconnect` each picked a control port with `with socket.socket() as s: s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))` and closed the socket straight away. The engines bind those ports seconds later, inside `P2PSecondaryTierManager` -> `ZmqTransport` -> ROUTER `bind`: one in a spawned producer `LLM` and one in an in-process consumer `LLM`. In that window, any ephemeral bind or connect on the host can take the port, for example NIXL/UCX listeners, torch.distributed, or the other engine. This is a TOCTOU race. Both failing CI ports are in the Linux ephemeral range. The CI step runs pytest serially, so xdist is not the source of the competition.

The tier cannot just bind port 0 and read the port back afterwards. The P2P control identity is `host:port` (`_local_id` in `manager.py`), and the configured port is the address peers dial, so the port has to be known before the tier starts.

**Fix.** A new `reserve_ports` fixture keeps each probe socket bound to `127.0.0.1:0` with `SO_REUSEADDR`. It never calls `listen`, and an `ExitStack` holds the socket until teardown. The three call sites now use this fixture. While a socket holds the port, the kernel's port-0 and connect autobind skip it. libzmq's TCP listener also sets `SO_REUSEADDR`, and Linux allows two non-listening `SO_REUSEADDR` sockets on the same port, so the ROUTER bind in either engine still succeeds.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- The fix depends on Linux `SO_REUSEADDR` semantics and on libzmq setting `SO_REUSEADDR` on TCP listeners (libzmq 4.3.5 was verified here). Both hold on the CI Linux images. The change is platform-agnostic, so CUDA runners are unaffected.
- The separate `P2P session did not reach the expected state` flake in `tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestBidirectionalManager::test_lookup_expiry_allows_zmq_reconnect` (build [102037](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102037)) is not addressed here. Open PR #64060 (`ZMQ_ROUTER_HANDOVER`) already fixes it. The V1 KV Offload job needs both fixes to be stable.

**Duplicate-work check.** I searched open PRs for `test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e`, `kv_offload port Address already in use`, `p2p lifecycle flaky`, `reserve port zmq test` and `p2p e2e port race`. None fix this test. #64060 targets `test_manager.py` (a different test). #44813 changes `get_open_ports_list` in `vllm/utils` and does not touch kv_offload. #64511 changes the p2p accuracy and fault scripts, not this file.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Muse Spark] Load the model classes lazily so importing the package doesn't initialize CUDA
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Importing any `vllm.models.muse_spark` submodule (e.g. `common.vision`) also imported the NVIDIA Muse Spark model, which imports FlashInfer, which initializes CUDA at import. This PR resolves the package's model classes lazily, like `vllm.models.inkling`, so importing a submodule no longer touches CUDA.

## Claims

- Importing `vllm.models.muse_spark.common.vision` (and collecting `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_muse_vision_encoders.py`) no longer initializes CUDA in the importing process.
- This removes the root cause of the intermittent `Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess` failure of `test_mm_prefix_lm_pipeline_parallel` in `(L4) Distributed Models Shard 2/4` (e.g. builds 102677–102780 on main), which #67637 worked around by spawning that test's workers.
- No behavior change for loading the models: the registry and `from vllm.models.muse_spark import ...` resolve the same classes, picking `amd` on ROCm and `nvidia` elsewhere as before.

## Validation

GB200 (aarch64), Python 3.12, main at `bb23c0a81` with `requirements/test/cuda.in` installed. A small pytest plugin, loaded with `-p`, prints a stack trace on the first `torch.cuda._lazy_init()` / `torch._C._cuda_getDeviceCount()` call. After collection, it forks a child and reports `torch._C._cuda_isInBadFork()`. Each run uses the CI step's pytest command with `--setup-only`, so tests are collected and fixtures set up but no test body runs:

```bash
cd tests
PYTHONPATH=<plugin dir> pytest -p cudatrace -q -s -m "distributed(num_gpus=2)" --setup-only \
  models/multimodal --ignore models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper.py
```

<details>
<summary>main: CUDA initialized while collecting test_muse_vision_encoders.py</summary>

```
===== CUDATRACE lazy_init =====
  File "tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_muse_vision_encoders.py", line 15, in <module>
    from vllm.models.muse_spark.common.vision import (
  File "vllm/models/muse_spark/__init__.py", line 10, in <module>
    from .nvidia.dspark import MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM
  File "vllm/models/muse_spark/nvidia/dspark.py", line 39, in <module>
    from vllm.models.muse_spark.common.layers import (
  File "vllm/models/muse_spark/common/layers.py", line 17, in <module>
    from vllm.models.muse_spark.common.ops.fused_rmsnorm import fused_rmsnorm_fwd
  File "vllm/models/muse_spark/common/ops/fused_rmsnorm.py", line 11, in <module>
    from flashinfer.norm import gated_residual_rmsnorm as postnorm_gated_residual
  File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flashinfer/jit/env.py", line 395, in <module>
    FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_DIR: pathlib.Path = _get_workspace_dir_name()
  File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flashinfer/compilation_context.py", line 129, in __init__
    major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)
  File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 799, in get_device_properties
    _lazy_init()  # will define _get_device_properties
CUDATRACE after collection: forked child in bad fork = True
CUDATRACE after collection: parent initialized=True events=['lazy_init', 'getDeviceCount']
```

The same step with `--ignore .../test_muse_vision_encoders.py`, or collecting only that shard's files (`test_maverick.py`, `test_mm_prefix_lm.py`), leaves CUDA untouched (`bad fork = False`). Collecting `test_muse_vision_encoders.py` alone reproduces it.
</details>

<details>
<summary>This PR: CUDA untouched</summary>

```
=== RUN trace_muse_only        (test_muse_vision_encoders.py alone)
CUDATRACE after collection: forked child in bad fork = False
CUDATRACE after collection: parent initialized=False events=[]
=== RUN trace_full_step        (the whole CI step)
CUDATRACE after collection: forked child in bad fork = False
CUDATRACE after collection: parent initialized=False events=[]
=== RUN registry_resolve
MuseSparkForCausalLM vllm.models.muse_spark.nvidia.model
MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration vllm.models.muse_spark.nvidia.multimodal
MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM vllm.models.muse_spark.nvidia.dspark
from-import ok MuseSparkForCausalLM
MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration <class 'vllm.models.muse_spark.nvidia.multimodal.MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration'>
```
</details>

`pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_muse_vision_encoders.py` with this PR (same machine): `36 passed, 42 warnings in 211.02s`.

## Details

**Root cause.** `vllm/models/muse_spark/__init__.py` imported the platform's model modules eagerly. The NVIDIA ones import FlashInfer at module level (e.g. `common/ops/fused_rmsnorm.py`, `nvidia/ops/all_reduce_dual_norm.py`), and FlashInfer's `jit/env.py` calls `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` at import to name its workspace directory. That fully initializes CUDA, so torch marks every process forked afterwards as a bad fork. vLLM decides whether to spawn by checking `torch.cuda.is_initialized()`, which is False in such a child, so it forks the engine and workers, which then fail at `set_device`.

**Why the CI failure was intermittent.** The runtime-shard plugin doesn't import files the plan assigns to other shards, so shard 2's pytest process initialized CUDA only when the plan put `test_muse_vision_encoders.py` there (or left it unplanned).

**Fix.** Making the package `__init__` lazy covers every eager FlashInfer import under `nvidia/` at once, rather than making each one lazy. The model classes now load on first attribute access through a module `__getattr__`, which is the same pattern as `vllm/models/inkling/__init__.py`. `TYPE_CHECKING` imports keep static typing.

**Limitations.** Loading a Muse Spark model still imports FlashInfer and initializes CUDA, as it must. Only importing the package or its submodules got lighter. #67637's spawn workaround in `test_mm_prefix_lm_pipeline_parallel` can stay; it's harmless. I didn't add a test: checking for this needs a fresh GPU process, and the validation above covers it.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][PP] Stage hand-off on SDMA copy engines (--pp-sdma-handoff)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With pipeline parallelism, each step's intermediate tensors go from one stage to the next over NCCL send / recv. On ROCm that peer copy runs as a blit kernel on the sender's CUs, so it slows whatever the sender computes next to it: an 8192^3 bf16 GEMM on the sender runs 5.1x slower while a 201 MiB tensor is copied to the next GPU (table below). In a TP1 x PP2 prefill of MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, a 16384-token step hands off several such tensors on both stages' compute path.

This PR adds an opt-in hand-off on SDMA copy engines, `--pp-sdma-handoff` (`ParallelConfig.pp_sdma_handoff`, off by default). It applies to PP2 x TP1 on gfx950 (MI355X), eager (`cudagraph_mode` NONE), both stages on one node; with the flag set and any of these unmet, the worker raises at init.
- The receiving stage allocates 3 slots and shares them with the sender over CUDA IPC.
- A sender thread waits for the step's event, then copies each tensor into the step's slot on two SDMA engines (no CUs).
- The stages sync slot reuse through two counters in `/dev/shm`: `ready` (sender) and `freed` (receiver, once the step that read the slot has run on its GPU). Shapes and non-tensor entries still go through the PP group's object send; those sends are reaped against `freed` (a gloo isend `Work` reports `is_completed()` False until `wait()`).

Eager only, because a CUDA graph replay reuses its output buffers while the copy may still read them. PP2 only, because a middle stage would relay tensors that alias its receive slots.

Why ROCr's `hsa_amd_memory_async_copy_on_engine` over ctypes rather than a HIP API: on HIP 7.16 (vLLM's ROCm image), `hipMemcpyBatchAsync` with `hipMemcpyFlagExtPreferCE` still runs device-to-device peer copies as a blit kernel (the flag only steers host <-> device batches), and `hipMemcpyAsync(kind=hipMemcpyDeviceToDeviceNoCU)` picks SDMA engines whose peer copy fails on MI355X (HSA status 4097), so the runtime skips the copy while returning `hipSuccess`. Explicit engines 2 and 4 work.

## Claims

- Sender compute next to the hand-off copy: +411% with torch's peer copy (what NCCL's path costs too), +1.4% with this PR's SDMA copy, at 64.5 GB/s instead of 59.3 GB/s.
- The receiver gets the tensors byte for byte, also when it reads a slot late while later steps refill the other slots.
- End to end, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP1 x PP2 prefill (16384-token steps): +3.6% throughput and -3.4% mean TTFT over NCCL, each of 4 alternated rounds between +3.0% and +3.9%; gsm8k unchanged.
- Off by default; without the flag nothing changes.

## Validation

MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-40941f2c4ba96fba0a7e282a5355e89cd74d9ac5` (HIP 7.16.26361) with this PR's Python on top.

Copier cost, cuda:0 -> cuda:1, one 201 MiB bf16 tensor (16384 x 6144) copied in a loop while 8192^3 bf16 GEMMs run on the sender, then on the receiver:

| copier | GB/s | byte-exact | sender GEMM | receiver GEMM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| torch peer copy (`y.copy_(x)`) | 59.3 | yes | +411% | +4.7% |
| `hipMemcpyBatchAsync`, 8 descriptors | 64.9 | yes | +257% | +0.7% |
| `hipMemcpyBatchAsync` + `hipMemcpyFlagExtPreferCE`, 8 descriptors | 65.0 | yes | +257% | +0.5% |
| `hipMemcpyAsync(kind=hipMemcpyDeviceToDeviceNoCU)` | - | no (copy skipped) | 0% | 0% |
| **this PR (`copy_on_engine`, engines 2 + 4)** | **64.5** | **yes** | **+1.4%** | **+0.6%** |

- `pytest tests/distributed/test_pp_sdma.py` on 2 GPUs: 4 passed (the PP2 hand-off over 8 steps through 3 slots with a late reader; the metadata-send reaping on CPU, with fakes and with real gloo isends).
- pre-commit clean on the changed files.

End to end: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (MXFP4 experts), TP1 x PP2, `--enforce-eager`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, prefix caching off, NCCL vs `--pp-sdma-handoff` on the same 2 GPUs. Load: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 8` after a 16-prompt warm-up; 4 rounds, the side order flipped every round, a fresh server per side and round. Means over the rounds:

| metric | NCCL -> `--pp-sdma-handoff` |
|---|---|
| request throughput | 3.18 -> **3.29** req/s (+3.6%) |
| prefill throughput | 52.1K -> **53.9K** tok/s (+3.6%) |
| TTFT mean | 2427 -> **2345** ms (-3.4%) |
| TTFT median | 2451 -> **2361** ms (-3.7%) |
| TTFT p99 | 2892 -> **2787** ms (-3.7%) |

- Throughput gain per round: +3.8%, +3.5%, +3.0%, +3.9%; the NCCL side spans 3.175-3.183 req/s over its 4 rounds.
- gsm8k, first 200 test questions over chat completions (T 0): 193/200 with NCCL, 193/200 with `--pp-sdma-handoff`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Report only written blocks from fs tier store jobs
commits.pr_body: ## Overview Block files in the `fs` tier are named by content hash, so when a prefix that is already on disk gets stored again, `_store_block` skips the write. The job still reported the full batch in `transfer_bytes`, and it completed in microseconds, so the back-pressure detector saw a big, instant write every time this happened. This PR makes the tier report only the blocks it actually wrote. ## Claims - `transfer_bytes` now counts written blocks only, and is `0` when every block was already on disk. `BackpressureDetector.update` already ignores `num_bytes <= 0`, so these jobs stop feeding the EMA. - Nothing else changes: same bytes on disk, same job success, same lookup verdicts and KV events. The C extension path and the pure Python path report the same counts. ## Validation - `test_store_reports_only_newly_written_blocks` stores `[1, 2]`, then `[2, 3]`, then `[1, 2]` again, and checks the reported bytes are 2, 1 and 0 blocks and that block 2's file was never rewritten. Runs on both store paths. On `main` it reports 2 blocks every time. - `test_update_ignores_jobs_that_wrote_nothing` pins the detector behaviour the fix depends on. - `test_store_skips_block_published_after_filter` covers a block another writer publishes between the filter and the write, on both store paths. `test_store_accepts_block_published_by_another_writer` (#61390) now also asserts `transfer_bytes == 0`. - `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering`: 588 passed, 1 skipped. `pre-commit` is clean. - #61390 and #61780 have since merged; this is rebased on both. ## Details This is the normal flow of tiering, not an edge case. The CPU tier is smaller than the filesystem tier, so it evicts a prefix, the next request recomputes it, stores it to CPU, and the completion cascades to `fs` again. There is no existence check before the cascade, so on a warm filesystem most of what the detector sees are these skipped writes. They drag the EMA down and keep the fast path engaged right when the filesystem might actually be slow. The count comes from the writers themselves: Python `_store_block` returns whether it published the block, and `fs_io_C.batch_store_block` returns the number written instead of `None`. A block another writer publishes after the existence filter, or that wins the rename (EEXIST, #61390), is skipped and not counted; the store still succeeds. The Prometheus `WRITE_BYTES` and `WRITE_TIME` counters in `metrics.py` are computed from key count and are left alone here. AI assistance (Claude) was used. commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support n > 1 on /inference/v1/generate
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The Rust frontend's token-in/token-out route, `/inference/v1/generate`, rejects `sampling_params.n > 1` with `Only n=1 is supported.`, while the Python route returns one choice per sample. Clients that need several samples per prompt (for example RL rollouts) have to send `n` separate requests, which repeats prompt handling and multimodal preprocessing for every sample.

This PR adds `n > 1` to the route by reusing the parallel-sampling path the OpenAI routes already use on the Rust frontend.

## Changes

- **Fan-out:** the prompt and any media are prepared once, then submitted as `n` child engine requests through the shared `generate_prepared_n` path. Like Python's `ParentRequest`, child IDs are `{index}_{request_id}`, and a seeded request gives each child `seed + index` (wrapping), so samples differ but stay reproducible. A seed of `-1` stays unseeded.
- **Non-streaming:** all choices are collected concurrently and returned in index order in one response. Prompt-level fields come from the first choice, usage counts the prompt once and sums completion tokens, and per-request metrics are reported only for `n = 1`.
- **Streaming:** per-choice chunk streams are interleaved with their `index` set. Prompt metadata (`prompt_token_ids`, `mm_placeholders`) is sent once, on the first chunk, and the per-choice usage chunks are merged into one final usage chunk.
- **Validation:** matches Python. `n` must be at least 1 and at most `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES`. Unlike Python's generate route, `n` may exceed the engine's `max_num_seqs`: the samples queue in the scheduler, and `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES` already bounds `n`. Greedy sampling with `n > 1` is rejected, checked after generation-config defaults are applied. The route submits through `TextLlm::generate_prepared_n`, so it gets the shared greedy check.
- **Errors:** if submitting any child fails, the streams already submitted are dropped, which aborts their requests.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed PRs for "generate n", "parallel sampling", "inference/v1/generate n > 1" and "Only n=1". #58914 covers `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`, #66078 covers gRPC `GenerateStream`, and #52844 added the current rejection on this route. None adds `n > 1` to HTTP `/inference/v1/generate`.

## Test Plan

    cd rust
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy -p vllm-server -p vllm-text --all-targets
    cargo test -p vllm-text
    cargo test -p vllm-server --lib

New route tests:

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Audio] Treat zero decode limits as disabled
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`docs/usage/security.md` says setting a media limit to `0` disables it, but the audio duration and decoded-byte limits currently treat `0` as a hard cap. This change makes zero disable those per-audio limits consistently across SoundFile, PyAV, and TorchCodec while preserving the request-level decoded-byte budget.

## Claims

- `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=0` and `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_BYTES=0` disable their respective per-audio limits.
- The request-level `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DECODE_BYTES` limit still applies when the per-audio byte limit is disabled.
- Default and positive limit values keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

- On a DGX Spark (aarch64, Python 3.12.3), the full `tests/multimodal/media/test_audio.py` suite passed: **37 passed, 14 warnings** in 21.37 seconds.
- With zero-limit normalization disabled, the nine new regression cases failed in all nine cases, reproducing the original behavior.
- The relevant pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, typos, test tethering, mypy, SPDX checks, and forbidden-import checks.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- DGX validation used the branch's Python source with the machine's installed vLLM 0.31.0 native extensions and an isolated FFmpeg runtime for TorchCodec.
- No model evaluation was run because this change affects decode-limit handling, not model computation or output quality.

## Details

The backends received zero as a literal limit. As a result, any non-empty audio exceeded the duration or decoded-byte cap. The shared normalization treats zero as disabled (`None`) before decoding. When the per-audio byte limit is disabled, `AudioMediaIO` still uses the request-level byte budget as the decoder's bound when that budget is configured.

This follows the existing documentation that zero disables a media limit. Disabling both the per-audio and request-level limits removes those protections, which is not recommended for untrusted inputs. No documentation change is needed because this patch makes the implementation match the existing documented behavior.

This does not duplicate [PR #61173](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61173), which handles the compressed-file size limit `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB`. [PR #56304](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56304) addresses audio extraction in the Dots3 NOTE-specific path; this change fixes zero-limit handling in the shared audio decoders.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Start multi_process_parallel's Ray cluster with one CPU per rank
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the intermittent `RuntimeError: Timed out waiting for file /tmp/ray/session_.../gcs_server_port_...` in `:nvidia: (B200) [Nightly] Distributed` (`test_mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter[2]`, 2 of the last 12 nightlies, e.g. [102057](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102057); tracked in #67307). `multi_process_parallel` now starts its local Ray cluster with `num_cpus=world_size`.

## Claims

- Ray no longer starts one idle worker process per host CPU (224 on the B200 pods) on every `ray.init` in `multi_process_parallel`; it starts one per rank. The next test's Ray head node is no longer starved of CPU, and the GCS startup timeout no longer fires.
- Rank tasks are unchanged: all 25 callers use `@ray.remote(num_gpus=1, max_calls=1)` targets with the default 1 CPU and launch no nested tasks, so `world_size` CPUs is exactly enough.

## Validation

B200 CI on the diagnostics PR #67339. It ran `test_custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.py` several times in the B200 Distributed step, with a sampler recording host and container state during every `ray.init`.

| | `ray.init` calls | failed | load avg at `ray.init` | `ray.init` time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before ([102363](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102363)) | 6 | 1 (the CI error) | 1,312–2,279 (from the 2nd call on) | 5.2–5.4 s |
| this fix ([102385](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102385)) | 20 | 0 | 9–31 | 4.3–7.4 s |

GB300 node (144 CPUs), Ray 2.56.1, four back-to-back `ray.init` → 2 tasks → `ray.shutdown` cycles:

| | Ray worker processes after `ray.init` | host CPU per cycle |
|---|---|---|
| before | 147 | 143–158 core-s |
| `num_cpus=2` | 5 | 24–35 core-s |

`:nvidia: (B200) [Nightly] Distributed` is `optional` and does not run on this PR's CI; the runs above are from #67339.

## Details

**Root cause.** Ray starts the raylet with `--num_prestart_python_workers=num_cpus` (`python/ray/_private/services.py`), launches them all at once when the first driver registers (`WorkerPool::HandleJobStarted`), and `ray.init` waits for them to register. The CI pod has no CPU limit (`cpu.max = max`), so Ray counts all 224 host CPUs. Every `ray.init` in `multi_process_parallel` therefore spawned ~224 `ray::IDLE` processes for a 2-rank test.

**Failure timeline** (from the sampler in 102363). The previous test's cluster was still tearing down its ~200 workers when the next `ray.init` started:
- the pod was using ~200–240 cores and 5,600 threads were waiting to run on 224 CPUs;
- the new `gcs_server`'s main thread was runnable throughout but got 0.6 s of CPU in its first 9 s;
- it missed Ray's fixed 30 s wait for its port file (`wait_for_persisted_port`, not configurable).

There was no cgroup throttling (`nr_throttled` 0) and no I/O or memory stall.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Raising the timeout: it isn't configurable, and only makes the starvation less likely to cross the window.
- A retry: ruled out by `tests/AGENTS.md`.
- Replacing Ray with multiprocessing (#67355): much larger.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][ROCm][DSv4.1] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: dense MXFP8 GEMMs and wo_a on AITER's tuned FlyDSL kernels, and a faster MXFP8 activation quant (MI355X)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash served as DP8 attention + EP8 MoE (TP1 dense linears) on 8x MI355X runs its 32x32 block-scaled MXFP8 linears on the Triton block32 GEMM. That GEMM has no TP1 tuning (`_default_config`) and reaches 21-31% of MXFP8 peak. On gfx950 with AITER enabled, this PR runs those linears and the grouped `wo_a` BMM on AITER's FlyDSL GEMMs, which AITER picks per M from its tuned tables. It also makes the MXFP8 activation quant about 2x faster, with bit-identical output.

## Claims

- **End to end** (InferenceX aiperf agentic, CONC=256, DSpark 5 tokens): **throughput_per_chip 26,714 tok/s/GPU, P90 interactivity 4.61 tok/s/user**. Both are within run-to-run noise of the previous revision of this PR on the same node (27,385 / 4.60), which measured +11.1% / +10.9% over main.
- **Dense GEMMs offline**, weighted by the calls per engine step of the profiled run: **prefill 189.8 -> 106.7 ms per step (1.78x)**, **decode 4544 -> 2822 us per step (1.61x)**.
- **MXFP8 activation quant**: 357 -> 172 us at M = 32768, K = 8192.
- **No extra memory**: weights are preshuffled in place, so the model stays at 52.1 GiB per GPU.
- **Accuracy unchanged**: GSM8K 0.9735 (main) vs 0.9727 (this PR), strict-match, ±0.0045.

| GEMM (N x K) | prefill M=32768, main -> PR (us) | speedup | decode weighted, main -> PR (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wq_b (32768 x 1280) | 2420 -> 1413 | 1.71x | 16.16 -> 11.84 | 1.36x |
| wo_a (G=8, 8 x 1024 x 4096) | 1995 -> 956 | 2.09x | 13.13 -> 10.47 | 1.25x |
| wo_b (5120 x 8192) | 1980 -> 1128 | 1.76x | 35.94 -> 16.86 | 2.13x |
| shared expert gate_up (4608 x 5120) | 1155 -> 688 | 1.68x | 24.63 -> 12.33 | 2.00x |
| shared expert down (5120 x 2304) | 565 -> 373 | 1.51x | 10.77 -> 7.68 | 1.40x |
| fused wq_a\|wkv (1792 x 5120) | 611 -> 342 | 1.79x | 9.10 -> 8.64 | 1.05x |
| indexer wq_b (4096 x 1280) | 280 -> 214 | 1.31x | 6.06 -> 5.41 | 1.12x |
| engram (25600 x 6144) | 6921 -> 3890 | 1.78x | 53.01 -> 32.50 | 1.63x |

Linear timings include the activation quant; `wo_a` takes an MXFP8 input. Measured with HIP-graph replay over rotating weight copies on one MI355X, AITER v0.1.29.

## What changes

- **`RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`**: a layer qualifies when AITER linear is on, the GPU is gfx950, the model is bf16, the weight has 32x32 scale blocks with K % 64 == 0, and AITER has tuned 32x32 rows for its shape (`rocm_aiter_ops.is_mxfp8_block32_bpreshuffle_gemm_tuned`). Such a layer is (16, 16)-preshuffled in place at load and exposed as `layer.weight_preshuffled`.
- **`rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm(_quant)`**: given `weight_preshuffled`, calls AITER's `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`. The FlyDSL kernels use 32-bit offsets, so rows run in 2 GiB chunks. Without it, the existing Triton paths are unchanged.
- **`rocm_dsv41_mxfp8_wo_a_bmm`**: given `weight_preshuffled`, calls AITER's `batched_gemm_a8w8_mxscale_bpreshuffle`.
- **Mono decode (gfx950)** reads the dense linears row-major. When it is selected, it marks the linears it reads with `keep_row_major_weight`; those keep their weight and get a preshuffled copy.
- **`_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel`**: each program handles a [4, 512] tile instead of one [64, 32] block. The arithmetic is unchanged.
- **Unchanged paths**: every other layer and configuration — 1x32-scaled models, untuned shapes, non-gfx950 including gfx1250, AITER off, and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`.

## Validation

**End to end.** Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-f5d93296`; this revision and the previous revision of this PR (explicit tier tables) alternate on one node.

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE
export HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1 MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=64G
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --port 6100 \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe --block-size 128 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false,"embedding_across_dp":true}' \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --prefill-schedule-interval 96 --long-prefill-token-threshold 8192 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# client: InferenceX `python3 -m infx.bench agentic` (aiperf), CONC=256, fast mode (1200 s)
```
