commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Fill dummy FP8 weights with random codes across the range
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Dummy FP8 weights (`--load-format dummy`) are now random finite codes across the FP8 range,
instead of values in ±1, so dummy-weight benchmarks of compute-bound steps match real weights
on power-capped GPUs.

## Claims

- On GB200 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4), dummy-weight timings of large prefill steps were up to
  11% faster than real weights. With this change they agree within run-to-run noise.
- An explicit `low`/`high` still samples uniformly. FP8 values are always finite (no NaN/Inf
  codes, for all four `float8` dtypes), deterministic for a seed, and filled in place, with no
  FP16 staging tensor.

## Validation

24 real serving prefill steps (busiest DP rank 870 to 49K tokens), each timed with
`vllm bench forward` under three weight setups:

| weights | vs real weights, mean \|diff\| | bias | worst |
|---|---|---|---|
| current dummy (±1) | — | — | −11.4% (≈ −10% on steps of 10K+ tokens) |
| this PR | 1.57% | +0.94% | 3.1% |

The same steps repeated on different nodes vary by 0.9%.

By step size, the gap of the current dummy grows with step length: −1.4% at <2K tokens, −10%
at 16K–70K. That's where the busiest GPUs sit at the ~1.1 kW power cap.

On two of these steps, on the same node with `nvidia-smi` logging, both dummy and real runs hit
the cap (throttle reason SW power cap). Real weights then ran at lower clocks: busiest GPU
p10/p50 1339/1950 MHz, against 1569/2062 MHz with the current dummy weights. Compute-bound
kernels were 5–20% slower and the memory-bound engram lookup was about the same.

The timings above used an equivalent prototype of this change; the only difference was that
NaN codes were decremented instead of zeroed.

Correctness: Qwen3-4B-FP8 with `--load-format dummy` running this branch generates with finite
prompt and sample log-probabilities (416 values, all finite).

Tests:

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py   # 67 passed
```

## Details

Real checkpoints scale FP8 weights to use the whole E4M3 range. In layer 10 of
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, the FP8 weights have std ≈ 85–100 and absmax 448, with block scales ≈
2^-12. Values uniform in ±1 hit only a few exponent codes, so the tensor-core operands toggle far
fewer bits. GEMM power follows operand bit activity, and under a power cap the GPU then holds
higher clocks than with real data.

FP4 and int8 dummy weights were already random bytes and matched real weights; only FP8 was
narrow. FP8 *block scales* (e.g. ModelOpt NVFP4 linear layers) without a pinned
`dummy_weight_value` also become full-range. Dequantized weights stay bounded by the dummy global
scales (±1e-3), and real checkpoints use the FP8 range for those scales too. NVFP4 MoE scales
that are pinned with `dummy_weight_value` are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue changes the dummy FP8 value range.

Decode steps keep their CUDA graphs when `--dbo-decode-token-threshold` is above the decode batch. - **All-reduce hand-off.** `init_dbo_tp_comms` builds one `PyNcclCommunicator` per microbatch and installs a hook in `GroupCoordinator._all_reduce_out_place`. That function runs under the `vllm.all_reduce` custom op, so compiled graphs reach the hook. Inside a microbatch thread the hook yields to the other microbatch, runs the all-reduce on the comm stream over that microbatch's communicator, and switches back; elsewhere it returns `None` and the normal path runs. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep dummy-run requests within max_model_len
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`_dummy_run` can build dummy requests longer than `max_model_len`. Attention then reads block ids past the end of the block table row during warmup, which can crash engine startup. This PR caps the dummy batch at `num_reqs * max_model_len` tokens. It follows up on #49751.

## Claims

- Warmup dummy runs no longer read past the block table when `max_num_batched_tokens > max_num_seqs * max_model_len`.
- This fixes a startup crash with, for example, `--max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 1 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, and the latent out-of-bounds read behind `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT` in `FlashAttnFwdSm90` in `test_auto_fit_max_model_len_rejects_oversized_input`.
- Configs where the cap does not apply run the same dummy batches as before.

## Validation

All GPU runs on one H200, `JackFram/llama-160m`, main at 379a8487a.

Minimal reproducer (no auto-fit involved):

```python
from vllm import LLM

if __name__ == "__main__":
    llm = LLM(
        "JackFram/llama-160m",
        max_model_len=2048,
        max_num_seqs=1,
        max_num_batched_tokens=8192,
    )
    print(llm.generate("Hello")[0].outputs[0].text)
```

vLLM accepts this config with a warning. Warmup then builds one 8192-token dummy request against a block table row sized for 2048 tokens:

```
WARNING [scheduler.py:406] max_num_batched_tokens (8192) exceeds max_num_seqs * max_model_len (2048). This may lead to unexpected behavior.
INFO [kernel_warmup.py:481] Running FlashInfer autotune with 8192 tokens and token buckets (1, 2, ..., 4096, 8192).
ERROR [core.py:184] torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

| Arm | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| main | 3 | 3 crash at startup (illegal memory access) |
| PR | 3 | 3 start and generate |

Runs were interleaved, each with a fresh `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`. The crash needs an out-of-range value in the stale memory after the row, so other GPUs or allocator states may not fault even though the read is out of bounds.

Block table row width against entries read by attention in the autotune dummy run:

| Config | Arm | Dummy request | Row width | Entries read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto-fit, `max_model_len` 2048 -> 32 | main | 1 x 2048 | 8 | 128 |
| auto-fit, `max_model_len` 2048 -> 32 | PR | 1 x 32 | 8 | 2 |
| explicit config above | main | 1 x 8192 | 128 | 512 |
| explicit config above | PR | 1 x 2048 | 128 | 128 |

Forced fault: with every entry past the row set to an out-of-range block id and `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, main faults in the autotune dummy run with the FlashAttention, FlashInfer and Triton attention backends. With this PR all three pass, in both configs.

Tests:

- New `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_dummy_run_requests_fit_in_max_model_len`: 2 of 4 cases fail on main (`[[2048]] != [[32]]`, `[[4096, 4096]] != [[2048, 2048]]`), 4 pass with this PR.
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_context_length.py`: 3 passed.
- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`: 36 passed. `test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py`: 67 passed.

Default config (`max_num_seqs` 256, `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384): the autotune dummy run is identical on main and with this PR (16384 tokens, 256 requests, same bucket list).

## Details

Root cause: `_dummy_run` splits `num_tokens` over at most `max_num_reqs` requests. #49751 spread the tokens evenly, but nothing bounds the per-request length when `num_tokens > max_num_reqs * max_model_len`. Block tables hold `max_model_len` tokens per request, so a longer dummy request makes attention read stale memory past the row as block ids. Whether that faults depends on the stale values, which is why it is intermittent in CI.

Two ways to get there:

- `--max-model-len auto`: auto-fit lowers `max_model_len` after `max_num_batched_tokens` was derived from the original value.
- Explicit settings. vLLM accepts them with a warning.

Because of the second case, lowering `max_num_batched_tokens` in auto-fit would not be enough, so the cap is in `_dummy_run`, which covers every caller.

Limitations:

- When the cap applies, the FlashInfer autotune bucket list is still built from `max_num_batched_tokens`. I left `kernel_warmup.py` unchanged to keep the fix small.
- When the cap applies, `profile_run` profiles fewer tokens, which matches what serving can schedule.
- CUDA graph capture builds its own dummy batches and is not touched. I did not test user-set capture sizes above `max_num_seqs * max_model_len`.
- Not run: elastic EP and ROCm AITER warmups (they go through `_dummy_run`), and the MLA, sparse and Mamba backends.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Allow non 8-bytes aligned `--max-num-batched-tokens` for DeepSeek-v4
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Model Runner V2 keeps all KV cache groups' slot mappings in one `[num_kv_cache_groups, max_num_batched_tokens]` int64 tensor, and DeepSeek-V4's CuTe DSL compressor, which declares `slot_mapping` 64-byte aligned (each element is 8 bytes, so `max_num_batched_tokens` is supposed to be 8 byte aligned), fails at engine init with "Misaligned Tensor data on argument #3", e.g., with --max-num-batched-tokens 1500 or 2500.

This PR pads the row stride of the slot-mapping buffers to 16 elements so every row starts 128-byte aligned, keeping the same layout.

## Claims

After this PR, `--max-num-batched-tokens` for DeepSeek-v4 supports any values.

## Validation

This PR is verified end-to-end for `GSM8K` on both H20 and DGX Sparks and should work for other cards as well.

## Details

See above. Note: the code is assisted by Claude Code
